draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Gopalaswamy Betta! At 1450m this is the highest peak in Bandipur National Park, and fog hangs over it all year, which is why it's called Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat up here, so bring water and snacks with you.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Gopalaswamy Hills and the Venugopalaswamy temple are about a 9 min walk from here.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot on the wooded slopes and watch the fog roll over the hills.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The hill sits right in the core of Bandipur National Park, and wild elephants wander around here.

legends.title: The hill in the mist
legends.body: Fog covers these hills nearly all year round, so locals added Himavad to the name. Put that together with the Venugopalaswamy (Krishna) temple and you get Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta.

tips.title: Expect fog.
tips.body: Dense fog sits on the hills round the year, so views come and go and it can feel cool.

tips.title: Stay alert for elephants.
tips.body: This is the core area of Bandipur National Park and elephants are frequent visitors.

story.title: A temple to Krishna
story.body: On top of the hill is the temple of Venugopalaswamy, a form of Krishna. The hill took its name from him.

story.title: The village below
story.body: Hangala, the Gundlupet taluk village 18 km from the hills, counted 5,597 people in the 2001 census.

story.title: Peak of Bandipur
story.body: Gopalaswamy Betta is the highest peak in Bandipur National Park, thickly wooded and wrapped in fog. Elephants and other wildlife roam all around it.
